inputs.root_cause: Surveyed xliff's remaining unresolved obligations for a fresh, well-scoped cluster after the UBL-WRITE-001 tick. Found SAL-XLIFF-OBL-AD191413B05A60ED (XLIFF-MODEL-001) stuck at status=missing with a stale missing_behavior claim ('no shipped-namespace test builds a multi-file document, so file-id-unique-within-document is never exercised') that was already false: its cross-capability duplicate SAL-XLIFF-OBL-087892B36F8591FF (XLIFF-PARSE-001, identical rule_text) was already status=implemented, citing exactly the multi-file-document tests the stale text claimed did not exist. Neither sibling, however, had direct test coverage for the other two clauses the shared rule_text bundles: 'one or more file elements' (xliff.file.required) and 'each carrying an id attribute' (xliff.file.id.required).
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-AD191413B05A60ED (missing->implemented) and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-087892B36F8591FF (already implemented, evidence strengthened to cover all 3 clauses directly)
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 2 new tests prove: a document with zero file elements is flagged xliff.file.required; a file element with no id attribute is flagged xliff.file.id.required. Both diagnostics already existed in validator.py, confirmed via direct interactive probing before writing any test.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed xliff's remaining unresolved obligations (48 unresolved of 142) grouped by capability_id, looking for a genuinely small, closeable cluster rather than the larger open-ended module/parse work already exhausted across 8 prior consecutive ticks this session (events 220-230).

2. Found SAL-XLIFF-OBL-AD191413B05A60ED at status=missing, whose rule_text is byte-identical to SAL-XLIFF-OBL-087892B36F8591FF (already status=implemented). Cross-checked exact rule_text equality directly against the obligation register (not the evidence file's own summary text) per the evidence-integrity discipline established earlier this session -- confirmed a true duplicate pair, not a superficially-similar-but-distinct obligation.

3. Read the missing obligation's own missing_behavior text: 'no shipped-namespace test builds a multi-file document, so file-id-unique-within-document is never exercised.' Read the implemented sibling's implemented_behavior and positive_test_selectors and found they cite tests/python/xliff/test_obligation_file_and_group_id_uniqueness.py::test_a_real_multi_file_document_with_distinct_file_ids_is_valid and ::test_two_files_sharing_an_id_are_flagged_as_duplicate -- both of which DO build multi-file documents and DO exercise file-id uniqueness, directly contradicting the missing obligation's own stale claim.

4. Read the full existing test file to confirm precisely what was and was not covered: uniqueness (clause 3) was fully covered by 2 existing tests; 'one or more files' (clause 1) and 'each file carries an id' (clause 2) had zero test coverage in either obligation's evidence.

5. Probed both untested clauses directly against the shipped package before writing any test: loads()+validate() on a document with zero <file> elements produced diagnostic code xliff.file.required; loads()+validate() on a document with one <file> element lacking an id attribute produced xliff.file.id.required. Both already existed in validator.py (lines ~613-622), confirmed by reading the source directly rather than assuming from the probe alone.

6. Extended the existing test_obligation_file_and_group_id_uniqueness.py (rather than creating a new file) since it already explicitly named both obligations in its own docstring and its docstring already documented the exact 3-clause bundling this tick closes -- adding a new file would have fragmented directly related coverage. Updated the docstring to record the later-slice rationale.

7. Added 2 new tests: test_a_document_with_zero_file_elements_is_flagged_as_invalid, test_a_file_element_without_an_id_attribute_is_flagged_as_invalid. Both passed on the first attempt -- zero source code changes needed.

8. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (447 passed, was 445, +2), and the full 6-format regression (3373 passed, was 3371, +2; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
9. No skills-first governance invocation needed -- zero src/ files changed, only an extended test file and evidence YAML, matching the 'skipped when only tests/evidence YAML change' rule.

10. Promoted SAL-XLIFF-OBL-AD191413B05A60ED to implemented (all 3 of its rule_text's clauses now individually, directly proven) and strengthened SAL-XLIFF-OBL-087892B36F8591FF's evidence (already implemented) to cite the same 2 new tests, correcting its own evidence from 'uniqueness proven, other two clauses proven only by implication' to 'all 3 clauses directly proven.'
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3373 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3371 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule; every claim verified by direct code inspection and interactive probing of already-shipped behavior.

Its cross-capability duplicate SAL-XLIFF-OBL-087892B36F8591FF (XLIFF-PARSE-001) remains implemented but now has strengthened, fully-direct evidence for all 3 of its rule_text's clauses instead of 2 of 3.
